For reference, Run 1's aggressive settings reached 97.1% mean coverage (uncapped depth range, different bag) — this run's 94.3% is lower partly because coverage is now measured only within ≤5m (a stricter bar; far-range fills that would have counted before don't count here) and partly because moderate settings genuinely fill fewer holes than maxed-out ones. That trade is the point of this run.

Edge sharpness the actual question this run asks

At locations Canny edge detection flags in the RGB image (a proxy for real object boundaries), the depth gradient magnitude (Sobel) is compared before vs. after filtering, restricted to locations whose full 3×3 neighborhood is valid in both frames (never a hole boundary mistaken for an edge). Ratio ≈1 = edge preserved as-sharp; <1 = blurred/softened; >1 = steeper than before.

Edge sharpness ratio0.976mean, after/before depth-gradient at RGB edges
Median ratio0.979typical frame
Depth gradient, before13.75cm/px, at RGB-edge locations
Depth gradient, after13.44cm/px, same locations
Edge pixels evaluated8702mean per frame
Reading this number: a ratio of 0.976 means depth transitions at RGB-detected edges are, on average, about as steep after filtering as before — edges are being preserved, not blurred, at moderate settings. This is measured on the same bag/settings actually used, not inferred from the flat-region roughness metric — see the caveats below for what this metric does and doesn't prove.

Flat-region roughness 3×3 only, for continuity with run 1

Roughness before (3×3)0.62 mmreal measurements, ≤5m

For comparison, Run 1's aggressive settings produced a +171% change at this same 3×3 scale (on a different bag/range). This run's smaller shift is consistent with moderate settings costing less flat-region smoothness, as intended.

Caveats

Edge sharpness is a proxy, not ground truth. Canny-detected RGB edges include some texture-only edges (not real depth boundaries), which dilutes rather than biases the signal — there's no independent higher-precision depth reference for this bag to validate against directly.

Different bag from Run 1, so the two reports' absolute numbers (coverage %, roughness mm) are not a strict controlled A/B of aggressive-vs-moderate on identical data — a true head-to-head would rerun both parameter sets on the same bag. This run is the direct answer to "what does moderate get us," not a rerun of run 1 with one setting changed.

Coarse (9×9) roughness was not recomputed this run — it was the most expensive part of Run 1's analysis, and this run's ask was specifically about edges, not re-litigating flat-region noise at multiple scales.
